title: Social media literacy: fake news consumption and perception of COVID-19 in Nigeria
screen_reason: Despite the title, the survey (108 Nigerian polytechnic students, Google Form circulated via WhatsApp and Facebook) never asks whether respondents encountered, consumed or shared fake news. The section headed 'Fake news consumption on the social media' (Table 5) in fact measures a preference for news on social media ('I prefer reading/watching/listening to news and information posted on social media'), not consumption of fake news. The two items about falsehood are belief items ('Coronavirus was prepared in a laboratory to target certain countries', 'Corona virus really exists'), and belief in false claims is explicitly outside scope. The one environment-perception item, Table 7 ('There are misleading information about COVID-19 on social media'), is reported only as separate agreement categories (Agree 44, 40.7%; Strongly Agree 32, 29.6%); the paper never states the combined share, and adding the two categories would be a cross-category sum, which R8 forbids. No extractable estimate remains. See missed_or_uncertain: this is the judgement call on this paper.
missed_or_uncertain: JUDGEMENT CALL for the adjudicator. Table 7, 'There are misleading information about COVID-19 on social media' (N = 108): Agree 44 (40.7%), Strongly Agree 32 (29.6%), Neutral 22 (20.4%), Disagree 6 (5.6%), Strongly Disagree 4 (3.7%). A coder who reads INSTRUCTIONS §1 ('Perceived amount of misinformation in one's environment (a lot / some / none) counts') broadly could keep this as a RECALL row at 70.3% agreeing or strongly agreeing. I did not, for two reasons: (a) the item is an agree/disagree statement about whether misleading COVID-19 content exists on social media, not a report of the respondent's own encounters and not an amount scale, so it sits outside the encountered/came across/received wording of the RECALL definition; (b) the combined 70.3% is nowhere stated in the paper and would have to be summed across two Likert categories, which R8 bans. If the adjudicator judges (a) satisfied, the row would be: Nigeria, multi_platform, RECALL/exposure, value 70.3, denominator 108 students, topic covid19, ground_truth self_report, sampling_frame convenience, borderline true. Also considered and rejected: Table 8 'Coronavirus was prepared in a laboratory to target certain countries' (37.0% agree, 18.5% strongly agree) and Table 9 'Corona virus really exists' (47.2% agree, 27.8% strongly agree, 8.3% disagree) — belief in false or true claims, explicitly excluded; Table 5 news preference (57.4% agree, 25.0% strongly agree); Tables 3 and 4 media-literacy behaviours (52.8% and 28.7% check sources per the Table 3 caption; 50.0% agree and 30.6% strongly agree they check the date; 3.7% disagree); Table 6 time on social media (28.7% more than 5 hours daily); Tables 10 and 11 preventive behaviour; demographics (76.9% male, 80.6% aged 18-25); and the externally cited Powell (2018) figure of 60.9% and the NOIPolls figures (95%, 49%), which are quoted from other sources and barred by R8. Data quality caveat the adjudicator should see: Table 3 is broken — its caption reports source-checking (52.8%, 28.7%) but its body is a verbatim duplicate of Table 4's date-checking item (50.0%, 3.7%, 15.7%, 30.6%), so the 52.8%/28.7% figures have no table behind them. Several results paragraphs are duplicated verbatim, and the concluding sentence points the reader to Tables 10 and 11 for a claim about gender.

rob.design: Descriptive cross-sectional survey, quantitative. Google Form link shared purposively via WhatsApp and Facebook with students of two institutions (Federal Polytechnic Mubi and Adamawa State Polytechnic), Nigeria; 108 responses analysed in SPSS with descriptive statistics and t-tests. Data-collection dates are not reported (article received 28 April 2022). No sampling frame, no response rate, no denominator for the invitation, no reliability or validity evidence for any item, no scale construction, and no coding of content (all measures are single self-report items). The paper describes its own sampling as both convenience (Abstract) and purposive (Methods). Several tables are mislabelled or duplicated.
